name: BLS International Services Ltd
_note: Fact base for the BLS initiation, as of 30-Sep-2026 (Q1FY27 basis). Rs crore unless stated. Every number has src and published date; only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

ar26.note: Annual Report 2025-26, sent with the notice of the 23-Sep-2026 AGM

hc.note: W.P.(C) 16352/2025, BLS International Services Ltd v. Union of India, Justice Sachin Datta

profile.what: Technology-enabled outsourcing partner to governments. Two reported segments: Visa & Consular Services (visa application centres for 46 client governments in 100+ countries, consular and citizen services, value-added services, Citizenship Invest (investment migration, Dubai), iDATA (Turkey; German and Italian missions), a UK hotel, and from FY27 the UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendras) and Digital Services (BLS E-Services Ltd, listed, 51% owned at Mar-26: business-correspondent banking for SBI and others through ~1.58 lakh touchpoints, assisted e-services, Aadifidelis loan distribution (57%), Zero Mass (90.9%), Starfin, and Atyati Technologies from Jul-2026).
profile.model: User-pay: the applicant pays a service fee per application plus optional value-added services (premium lounge, courier, SMS, form filling, insurance); the government pays nothing. Contracts typically run 5-10 years and are mostly exclusive by country/region. All visa centres are leased (asset-light); fees are collected upfront (negative working capital).
profile.scale: 44.1 lakh visa applications in FY26 (37.5 lakh in FY25); net revenue per application ₹3,302 (FY25 ₹2,903); ~10% of the outsourced visa market by volume and ~17% by value (2024, company estimate, ex-USA); 1,805 permanent employees at the parent (Mar-26).
profile.biggestClients: Spain (global contract since 2016, renewed 2023), Italy, Germany (via iDATA), Portugal, Poland, Slovakia (5-year global contract won FY26), Cyprus, Canada, India (MEA: Indian missions abroad, attestation and apostille, China VACs from Oct-2025). Indian missions were ~12% of consolidated revenue and ~8% of EBITDA in Q1FY26 (company, Oct-2025).

shares.note: 41,17,40,908 shares of ₹1 (₹41.2 cr capital, Q1FY27 deck: 41.2 cr outstanding). A 1:3 bonus in FY23 took capital from ₹10 cr to ₹41 cr. No issue between Mar-26 and Sep-26.

q1fy27.notes: Record quarter: revenue +25.3%, EBITDA +23.6%, PAT +11.4% (tax 14.4% vs 9.6%; D&A +39% on Aadhaar centres and leases). Visa volumes flat (11.3 lakh) despite the West Asia war; growth from net revenue per application (+11%), Citizenship Invest, the UK hotel and Aadhaar. Digital +32% (BC and loan distribution), margin 8.0% (7.3%). Net cash ₹1,617 cr (30-Jun-2026).

guidance.text: Organic growth target 15-20% a year for five years on the FY26 base (Aug-2026); FY27 internal target 20-25% (May-2026). Visa net revenue per application stabilising: revenue growth 12-15% (travel 7-8% + ~5%); 10-15% growth after contract expiries and wins (Aug-2026).
Maintain ~40% EBITDA margin in Visa & Consular and ~8% in Digital (with digital improving as it scales); 'subject to the mix'.

Work order ₹2,055 cr for Aadhaar Seva Kendras (6 years, user-pay), plus a ₹100 cr Bihar enrolment project. Capex ~₹125 cr in three phases (₹75 cr spent by Aug-2026); full revenue from Q4FY27-Q1FY28; ~₹2,500 cr of revenue over six years; EBITDA margin 10-15% (Aug-2026; 15-20% said in May-2026).
Effective tax rate ~12% for FY27 (Q1 14%); Dubai free-zone benefits; UAE rate change could add ~1 point.
Q1FY27 ₹32 cr; 'a little higher' in Q2 as the Aadhaar investment completes, then stable.

Organic expansion first, then M&A at 17-20% returns, then dividends; ~₹2,000 cr earmarked for acquisitions over 4-5 years (management interview cited on the May-2026 call); buyback 'not under consideration' but may be discussed by the Board (Aug-2026). Final dividend ₹0.50 (FY26 total ₹2.50, ~₹103 cr).

history.event: First visa contract (Portugal embassy, New Delhi).
Listed on NSE and BSE; won the global visa outsourcing contract for Spain (renewed in 2023).
Move from a partner-run to a self-managed model; Visa EBITDA margin 14.6% (FY22) to 22.1% (FY24) and 40.1% (FY26).
1:3 bonus issue (capital ₹10 cr to ₹41 cr). FY24: BLS E-Services IPO (Feb-2024; ₹296 cr raised by the subsidiary).
Citizenship Invest (Dubai, investment migration) bought for ₹260 cr; iDATA (Turkey; German and Italian visa centres) bought in FY25; FY25 acquisition outflow ₹899 cr (cash flow).
BLS E-Services bought 57% of Aadifidelis Solutions (loan distribution); ~25% of FY26 revenue.
MEA debarred BLS from new tenders of the Ministry and Indian missions abroad for two years (GFR Rule 151(iii)); existing contracts continued. Stock fell ~18% on 13-Oct-2025.

Delhi High Court (Justice Sachin Datta) quashed the debarment order; MEA left free to issue a fresh, specific show-cause notice only on alleged substandard service. No appeal or fresh notice found in public sources by 30-Sep-2026.
Won UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra order (₹2,055 cr), MEA China VACs (3-year), Slovakia global (5-year), Cyprus; UK hotel bought.
BLS E-Services completed the purchase of 100% of Atyati Technologies (BC network for non-SBI banks plus banking software) for ₹156.82 cr; FY26 revenue ~₹275 cr, EBITDA ₹20-21 cr.
BLS bought 2.21% more of BLS E-Services in the market for ₹45.22 cr.
